traits.plication.note: In every Coryphoideae, fan or feather (Phoenix, and the Caryoteae), the pleated blade splits along its upper folds, so each segment or leaflet is V-shaped, trough up (induplicate); Guihaia alone splits the other way (Dransfield et al. 2008, p. 16; Kaplan 2022, p. 489-492).

traits.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves usually induplicately palmate, less often pinnate (Phoenix, and Arenga and Caryota of tribe Caryoteae); the fan palms of dry and temperate country are here. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments, so it is counted simple and parted, its pattern palmate.
